To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the activity of developing neural circuits is stabilized by a set of synaptic plasticity rules that act to maintain the activity of neurons and circuits within a narrow window of activity; (2) homeostatic plasticities are not limited to development, but are also used by mature neural circuits to maintain activity levels in the face of changing inputs; and (3) homeostatic mechanisms may be important in a variety of processes ranging from memory consolidation to synaptic scaling in response to chronic activity changes

1) homeostatic synaptic scaling is a general mechanism for maintaining stable neuronal activity levels in the developing nervous systems; 2) homeostatic plasticities are crucial for the refinement of neural circuits; 3) homeostatic scaling is an important component of the cellular mechanisms that underlie long term potentiation; 4) homeostatic mechanisms are also involved in the maintenance of long term memory
homeostatic plastic mechanisms are essential for normal development of the nervous system and are also important for normal functioning of the mature brain.
